title: Jailer 2 Beats Leo in Kerala in Seven Days, Becomes Biggest Tamil Grosser in State
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel crossed Rs 60 crore gross in Kerala on Day 7, overtaking Vijay's Leo — and completing a sweep in which every major non-Malayalam industry's top Kerala grosser is now a sequel.
body:
• Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 crossed Rs 60 crore gross in Kerala in seven days, overtaking Vijay's Leo to become the highest-grossing Tamil film ever in the state, according to trackers.
  • Filmibeat, citing tracker AB George, put Jailer 2 at over Rs 60.1 crore against Leo at Rs 60 crore; Sacnilk put Leo's lifetime benchmark at Rs 59.65 crore and Jailer 2 at Rs 60 crore-plus in seven days.
  • The record means the top Kerala grosser from each of the Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi industries is now a sequel — Jailer 2, Baahubali 2, KGF Chapter 2 and Dhurandhar 2.
  • Jailer 2, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, released worldwide on October 15, 2026, with Rajinikanth reprising Tiger Muthuvel Pandian.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has become the highest-grossing Tamil film in Kerala, passing Vijay's Leo inside its first week. The milestone, reached on Wednesday, October 21 — the film's seventh day in theatres — underlines Kerala's weight as a market for Tamil cinema and the durability of the Rajinikanth-Vijay box-office rivalry outside Tamil Nadu.

How the Record Fell

According to Filmibeat, film industry tracker AB George reported in an X post at 7:31 PM on Wednesday that Jailer 2 had surpassed Leo's lifetime Kerala collection within seven days, and a later update placed the film at over Rs 60.1 crore, ahead of Leo at Rs 60 crore. Sacnilk reported the same record with slightly different tracker figures: Leo's lifetime benchmark at Rs 59.65 crore and Jailer 2 at Rs 60 crore-plus in seven days. Tracker estimates vary, but both place Jailer 2 at the top.

"Sacnilk reported the same record with slightly different tracker figures: Leo's lifetime benchmark at Rs 59.65 crore and Jailer 2 at Rs 60 crore-plus in seven days."

The Kerala Tamil-film record has changed hands repeatedly in recent years. Kamal Haasan's Vikram held a leading position before Rajinikanth's Jailer overtook it in 2023, and Leo then moved ahead of Jailer. Filmibeat's current ranking lists Jailer third at Rs 57.70 crore, followed by Vikram at Rs 40.10 crore and Coolie at Rs 25 crore.

A Clean Sweep for Sequels

Sacnilk noted a pattern in the new record: the highest-grossing Kerala film from each major non-Malayalam industry is now a sequel. Jailer 2 leads for Tamil cinema at Rs 60 crore-plus, Baahubali 2: The Conclusion holds the Telugu record at Rs 72.20 crore, KGF: Chapter 2 holds the Kannada record at Rs 65 crore, and Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge leads Hindi films at Rs 19 crore. Each arrived with an established franchise identity — a popular central character or an unresolved storyline — which matters in a market where other-language releases compete with a strong local Malayalam industry.

The Film and What Comes Next

Jailer 2 is the sequel to the 2023 hit Jailer. Nelson Dilipkumar returned as writer and director, Kalanithi Maran produced under Sun Pictures, and Rajinikanth reprises retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian. The cast includes Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu and Vidya Balan, with cameo appearances by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Hrithik Roshan, Jackie Shroff and Vijay Sethupathi. Anirudh Ravichander composed the music.

For diaspora audiences, Kerala is a useful proxy for the film's wider run: it opened with the biggest first day ever for a Tamil film in the state, and its worldwide run had already passed Rs 500 crore in six days. Attention now turns to its second week — how far past Leo's benchmark it can push, and whether it can challenge the all-industry Kerala marks set by Baahubali 2 and KGF Chapter 2.
